Global parameter altering quantum dispersion and energy scaling.

Model conventions: ℏ = 1. Energies, lengths, time, and frequencies use dimensionless model units. Unspecified phonon/KP lattice constants are 1; Coupled Wells uses the displayed distance d.

A narrower initial width spreads faster (Heisenberg uncertainty).

Sets the periodic normalization interval and spacing between allowed k values.

Animates an equal superposition containing every state from 1 through the selected n.

n = 1 is the ground state with one central antinode.

Energy levels scale inversely with L².

Tunneling probability drops exponentially with width.

a = 1 is unstrained; compression raises the kinetic-energy scale.

Positive values stretch the lattice; negative values compress it.

Sets the slope of the linear stress–strain relation in model units.

Controls periodic scattering and the resulting band gaps.

Controls the rate of the cyclic tensile–compressive loading.

Animates phase evolution or the coherent packet’s classical oscillation.

Selects pure state n and includes coherent components j = 0…n. Range: 0–80.

Range: 0.25–6.00. Sets the relative Poisson weights before the selected cutoff.

Controls the steepness of the parabolic potential well.

Compare an ordinary turn with the geared state’s ratio-dependent return.

Scales the central gear, its tooth count, and the planet’s orbital rate. The 1:1 ratio gives exact 4π behavior.

Jump to the initial state, one full turn, or the ratio-dependent return.

Controls playback rate without changing the rotation path.

Electrons accelerate opposite to the applied field.

Sets the width of the thermal velocity distribution.

A lightweight ensemble; reset after changing this value.

Use 0.1× for 10% playback speed.

Particles start as a tight cluster at x = 4. Drag −γx pulls the mean toward the origin while noise spreads the packet. Play then runs Anderson reverse from those same positions back toward the original cluster.

Larger γ relaxes the mean toward x = 0 faster and lowers D = T/γ.

Sets the noise strength through fluctuation–dissipation.

Histogram counts how many particles sit in each x bin.

Classical long-channel nMOS charge-sheet model. Plots use VGS and VDS; the textbook equations are evaluated with body-referenced potentials.

Surface potential uses solid drain-end and dashed source-side curves with separate orange and cyan tracers. The transfer view’s semilog plot shows total, drift, and diffusion components.

Identical atoms arranged in two-atom unit cells; even values up to 250.

Repeats the selected 2D lattice unit cell along both in-plane directions.

Stiffer bonds raise every vibrational frequency.

Every site in the spring model has this same mass.

K₂ = (K₂/K₁)K₁. Unequal alternating bonds open a frequency gap.

Effective transverse restoring force from bending, tension, or a substrate.

Controls the normal-mode playback rate.

Magnifies arrows only; it does not alter the atomic trajectory.

TO: ions move perpendicular to q and radiate. LO: ions pair along q and create a long-range longitudinal electric field, with no radiation.

Set Z*=0 for the nonpolar limit.

Selected cubic and tetragonal lattices, plus zinc blende.

Rotate and zoom both direct and reciprocal lattices independently.

The construction uses the selected structure's Bravais translation lattice.

Watch neighbor bisectors move inward and clip away points closer to another lattice site.

At completion, the central intersection is the primitive Wigner–Seitz cell.

The first zone is constructed as the reciprocal-lattice Wigner–Seitz cell.

Controls how many neighboring reciprocal points are shown around the zone.
